claims.sourceText: Nomination of Admiral B.R. Inman, hearing before the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, 97th Congress 1st session, 3 February 1981, GPO print 74-227 O, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/sites-default-files-hearings-97inman.pdf
claims.text: He gave his own career to the Senate: 'Subsequent assignments included service as the fleet intelligence officer on the staff of the commander, 7th Fleet; attendance at the National War College; executive assistant and senior aide to the Vice Chief of Naval Operations; assistant chief of staff for intelligence to the commander in chief, U.S. Pacific Fleet; Director of Naval Intelligence; and Vice Director for Plans, Operations, and Support of the Defense Intelligence Agency.'

claims.sourceText: Nomination of Admiral B.R. Inman, Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, 3 February 1981, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/sites-default-files-hearings-97inman.pdf
claims.text: He dates the NSA directorship himself and states the nomination: 'since July 5, 1977, I have had the pleasure of serving as Director, National Security Agency', and 'I have been nominated by the President to serve as the Deputy Director of Central Intelligence.'

edges.label: Nominated and heard as Deputy Director of Central Intelligence, 3 February 1981
edges.note: Nominated and heard on 3 February 1981 to be Deputy Director of Central Intelligence, the post SAIC's own proxy later lists among his government service.

edges.label: Vice Director for Plans, Operations and Support of DIA
edges.note: Vice Director for Plans, Operations and Support of the Defense Intelligence Agency before the NSA directorship, in his own testimony.

edges.label: Director of the National Security Agency from 5 July 1977
edges.note: Director of the National Security Agency from 5 July 1977, stated by him under oath at his 1981 confirmation hearing.
